book_evidence: body L5-10 states equality in distribution is equivalent to literal f_X=f_Y
source_evidence: transcript 150-300 gives the same classroom-level statement; no board dispute
math_analysis: Densities are determined only a.e.; changing a normal density at one point preserves every interval probability but breaks literal pointwise equality.
recommended_disposition: Use f_X=f_Y almost everywhere, or state a chosen canonical density version.
fidelity_note: The book faithfully carries over the source simplification, but the literal textbook claim is false.

book_evidence: body L109-124 differentiates the Gaussian integral under the integral sign
source_evidence: transcript 1801-2100 explicitly presents the Feynman parameter-differentiation method; board_009 OCR contains the same differentiated identity
math_analysis: The identity is correct. A dominated-differentiation argument near any fixed sigma>0 supplies the omitted rigor; this is a conventional pedagogical omission, not a faulty formula.
recommended_disposition: Optional one-sentence dominated-differentiation justification; no fidelity correction needed.

book_evidence: body L145-166 gives F_X(x)=1-e^{-lambda x}, tail=e^{-lambda x}, and scaling CDF without domain conditions
source_evidence: transcript 2400-2700 discusses the same formulas in elapsed-time context
math_analysis: For x<0 the CDF and tail are 0 and 1 respectively. Memorylessness/scaling calculation requires x,y>=0; the density at L136-142 already establishes the required piecewise support.
recommended_disposition: State piecewise CDF/tail and quantify the displayed calculation over x,y>=0.

book_evidence: body L191-199 says the probability/integral identity holds for every subset D
source_evidence: transcript 3627-3905 uses regions D, not a measurable-set qualification
math_analysis: Neither P(X in D) nor a Lebesgue integral is defined for an arbitrary nonmeasurable subset; Borel or Lebesgue-measurable D is required.

book_evidence: body L292-298 retains only existing expectations before displaying the variance-sum identity
source_evidence: transcript 5103-5400 expressly adds that the variances must exist
math_analysis: Finite first moments do not imply finite second moments. The equality needs finite variances/second moments in the ordinary finite-variance reading.
recommended_disposition: Restore the source's variance-existence condition in the statement and exercise.

book_evidence: body L331-366 formulates a density transformation only on the image and invokes the integral theorem for arbitrary measurable A under insufficiently specified domain/regularity hypotheses
source_evidence: transcript 5400-6300 states an informal two-dimensional version and proof; no stricter qualification is supplied
math_analysis: A full density needs zero off the image. The invoked multivariable theorem needs measurable domains and standard C1-diffeomorphism/a.e. hypotheses; those are not consequences of the written assumptions.
recommended_disposition: State the density piecewise and cite/formulate standard change-of-variables hypotheses.

book_evidence: body L490-499 sets W=X, then uses y=z/w and J=-1/w although its closed triangle includes x=w=0
source_evidence: No corresponding XY bounded-triangle example occurs in transcript 0-10280; board_018-028 cover only the sum/Gamma scheme
math_analysis: The map is noninjective on x=0 and inverse/Jacobian are undefined there. Restricting to x>0 removes only a null boundary and validates the otherwise correct density calculation.
recommended_disposition: Explicitly restrict to x>0 up to the null boundary, then define the density at z=0 arbitrarily.

book_evidence: body L594-612 uses beta in beta^alpha exp(-beta x) and mean alpha/beta, but L615 calls it a common scale parameter
source_evidence: transcript 7800-9001 uses the same rate convention and calls the second parameter fixed without calling it a scale
math_analysis: The displayed convention is rate; a scale-beta convention would use exp(-x/beta) and mean alpha beta.
recommended_disposition: Call beta the common rate/intensity parameter.

book_evidence: body L621-637 writes the convolution from 0 to y_2 and final Gamma form without restricting y_2
source_evidence: transcript 8403-8700 explicitly says y_2>0 and identifies the feasible geometry; board_026 OCR also labels y_2>0
math_analysis: For y_2<0 the feasible set is empty, not an oriented integral from 0 to y_2. The density must be zero there.
recommended_disposition: State calculation/result for y_2>=0 and f_{Y_2}=0 for y_2<0.
